newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG defence chief placed under house arrest.
newsitem.headline: PNG defence chief placed under house arrest.

text.p: Papua New Guinea soldiers on Monday placed the country's defence chief under house arrest, after freeing a jailed major who commanded an army revolt in March from a police cell.

Papua New Guinea defence force spokesman Colonel Jack Tuat told Reuters that army commander Colonel Leo Nuia had been placed under arrest inside the country's main defence headquarters Murray Barracks.
"Yes, the commander has been placed under house arrest," Tuat told Reuters. Tuat did not give any more details of the arrest, but added a briefing was planned later on Monday.
Major Walter Enuma, who was due to face firearm charges in court later on Monday, was freed from a Port Moresby police cell earlier on Monday by a small group of soldiers, police said.
The soldiers then returned to Murray Barracks and placed the army commander under house arrest.
In March, Papua New Guinea was rocked by an army revolt against the hiring of African mercenaries to end a secessionist rebellion on Bougainville island.
